findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD.

A tray of raw ground beef is observed stored on a shelf over containers of cooked ground beef used for sandwiches in the reach in cooler across from the hand washing station. The PIC was shown and rearranged the items during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that foods are stored so that cross contamination of pathogens is not a concern.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The nozzle used for root beer on the fountain drink machine is observed heavily soiled on the inner surface during his inspection. The PIC was shown and cleaned the nozzle during this inspection to correct. He stated that they are soaked regularly. This helps but routine cleaning is still needed to maintain safe standards. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-303.11 Ice Used as Exterior Coolant, Prohibited as Ingredient. After use as a medium for cooling the exterior surfaces of FOOD such as melons or FISH, PACKAGED FOODS such as canned BEVERAGES, or cooling coils and tubes of EQUIPMENT, ice may not be used as FOOD. 

A gallon of tea is observed stored in the ice in the ice machine during this inspection. The PIC was shown and removed the item during this inspection to correct. Ensure that ice used for drinks is not used as a cooling or cold holding medium.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

Allergen training is not available for the certified food protection manager (CFPM) during this inspection. This situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to renew prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD.

The PIC was shown and rearranged the items during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that foods are stored so that cross contamination of pathogens is not a concern.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

Wet wiping cloths are observed on the counters throughout the kitchen. There is a CL smell to the cloths indicating that they are used for sanitizing. This was discussed with the PIC and they moved the cloths back to the bucket to correct. Ensure that all wiping cloths used in the kitchen are stored between uses in solution at all times.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

Allergen training is not available for the certified food protection manager (CFPM) during this inspection. This situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to renew prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

On arrival the hand sink used for the kitchen was without paper towels. The PIC was notified and the towels were replaced during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Raw ground beef is observed over cooked beef and pickles in the refrigerator in the back. The PIC moved the items during the inspection to correct. Do not store raw meats over Ready-To-Eat foods in the coolers.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The nozzle of the root beer on the fountain drink machine is observed soiled. PIC indicated that they soak/clean the item weekly. This needs to take place more often. The item was cleaned during this inspection to correct. Ensure that it is cleaned often enough to prevent accumulation of slime/mold.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Raw ground beef is observed over cooked beef and pickles in the refrigerator in the back. The PIC moved the items as the inspector was looking at them. Violation corrected immediately.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. 

The ice scoop is observed soiled on the handle and is in need of cleaning. The PIC was shown and the scoop washed during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

A food employee was observed to not wash their hands prior to donning gloves and handling food. Education was conducted to correct.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-303.11: After use as a medium for cooling the exterior surfaces of FOOD such as melons or FISH, PACKAGED FOODS such as canned BEVERAGES, or cooling coils and tubes of EQUIPMENT, ice may not be used as FOOD. 

A pitcher of tea is observed stored in the ice in the ice machine during this inspection. PIC removed the pitcher immediately to correct the violation. Ice used for drinks should be protected from contamination from any source prior to use.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

Multiple moist rags are observed on counters throughout the kitchen. Wiping cloths should be stored between uses in their sanitizing solution. A discussion took place and the rags placed into the bucket or discarded to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

On arrival, the bucket of sanitizer for use in the kitchen did not register on the inspector’s test strips. PIC remade the solution to correct concentrations during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf).

A gallon of milk is observed in the refrigerator partially used and without a date marking. PIC indicated that the milk was opened Friday (2/10/23). This makes today day six of the seven for date marking. PIC placed a date marking on the milk during the inspection to correct the violation and they are instructed to ensure that date marking is maintained correctly for the TCS foods in the facility.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

The baffles of the hood system are observed heavily soiled with dust. The situation was discussed with the PIC. They said that the system is cleaned yearly. Inspector stated that cleaning of the baffles needs to take place between the times where a professional company makes scheduled visits. PIC instructed to remove and clean the baffles as needed to maintain them clean.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. [C]

Ceiling above the storage coolers & freezers observed to be damaged. PIC stated this is caused by leaks that have been fixed throughout the facility, but the source of the leak above the coolers has not been fixed. He indicated that the leak in question should be repaired over the summer. Eliminate leak and repair ceiling so it is smooth & easily cleanable.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
2nd REPEAT: Three wet wiping cloths observed on counters throughout the kitchen. Discussed with PIC, who stated that facility has switched to using a spray bottle of sanitizer. Cease use of wiping cloths with sanitizer spray bottle- use disposable paper towels with sanitizer spray bottle. Do not store damp cloths on the counter. They must be kept submerged in sanitizer solution.
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Ceiling above the storage coolers & freezers observed to be damaged. PIC stated this is caused by leaks that have been fixed throughout the facility, but the source of the leak above the coolers has not been identified. Eliminate leak and repair ceiling so it is smooth & easily cleanable.
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. [C]

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: Four-inch pan of ground beef observed covered, cooling on the counter. PIC stated that it began cooling at 10:45 or 11AM. At 1:30PM, the ground beef was 85F, probed. Discussed cooling practices and benchmarks. Foods must cool from 135F to 70F in two hours, and reach 41F in a total of six hours. CORRECTED- Food was voluntarily discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.14 (A) Cooked TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57ºC (135ºF) to 21ºC (70 F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57ºC (135ºF) to 5ºC (41 F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Four-inch deep pan of ground beef observed covered with a lid and a towel, cooling on the counter. When cooling food, separate into small portions, use shallow pans, and cover loosely (or not at all if safe from contamination). CORRECTED— Ground beef had not reached 70F within 2 hours of cooling, and was voluntarily discarded.
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans; Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. [C]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Pitcher of iced tea observed stored in the ice machine containing ice intended for use in beverages. CORRECTED— Iced tea removed. Ice intended for consumption cannot be used for cooling.
3-303.11: After use as a medium for cooling the exterior surfaces of FOOD such as melons or FISH, PACKAGED FOODS such as canned BEVERAGES, or cooling coils and tubes of EQUIPMENT, ice may not be used as FOOD. [P]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Two wet wiping cloths observed on counters throughout the kitchen. CORRECTED-- Discussed with PIC, who returned cloths to newly prepared sanitizer bucket. Do not store damp cloths on the counter. They must be kept submerged in sanitizer solution.
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. [C]

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Single-service forks and spoons observed stored in one bin, with forks going one direction and spoons going the other. Picking up a spoon would result on contamination of the eating end of a fork. CORRECTED— Provided education and discussed with PIC. Utensils rearranged to prevent potential contamination of food-contact portions.
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. [C]

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
Observed ice scooped using a cup with no handle. CORRECTED-- Discussed with PIC. Use a scoop with a handle to scoop. This prevents contamination of the ice from hands. Ice scoop is available. Proper use of ice scoop observed after discussion.
3-801.11: (D) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact READY-TO-EAT FOOD as specified under ¶¶ 3-301.11(B) and (E). [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed sandwiches prepared by placing the buns directly on the countertop that had not been sanitized or protected in any way from contamination. For example, inspector's clipboard had been set on that section of countertop just before sandwiches were prepared there. CORRECTED-- Provided education and discussed with PIC. Sanitize surfaces before using for food prep or use a barrier such as paper sandwiches will be wrapped in.
3-304.11: FOOD shall only contact surfaces of (A) EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned as specified under Part 4-6 of this Code and SANITIZED as specified under Part 4-7 of this Code. [P]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Six spray bottles observed either unlabeled, or labeled with "sanitizer." Contents of the bottles ranged in color (blue, purple, clear, and yellowish). CORRECTED-- PIC labelled spray bottles with their contents. Any bottles with unknown contents were discarded.
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Three wet wiping cloths observed on counters throughout the kitchen. CORRECTED-- Discussed with PIC, who returned cloths to newly prepared sanitizer bucket. Do not store damp cloths on the counter. They must be kept submerged in sanitizer solution.
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Sanitizer bucket that was presented upon arrival observed to be sudsy. PIC stated that it contained both Cl sanitizer and soap. Do not mix soap and sanitizer. CORRECTED-- Provided education. PIC prepared a bucket of Cl sanitizer ONLY (mixed with water) at a concentration of 100ppm. Sanitizer must be prepared during all times of food prep and service.
4-303.11: (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment: Bowl of ground beef observed cooling on the counter. PIC stated that it began cooling at 1PM. At 3PM, the ground beef was 100F, probed. Discussed cooling practices and benchmarks. Foods must cool from 135F to 70F in two hours, and reach 41F in a total of six hours. CORRECTED- Food was moved to shallow pans and placed in the freezer to rapidly cool.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.14 (A) Cooked TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57ºC (135ºF) to 21ºC (70 F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57ºC (135ºF) to 5ºC (41 F) or less. (P)

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment: Bowl of ground beef (mentioned in Violation 20) observed cooling on the counter, covered by deli paper without any cooling methods being used to bring food to 70F in 2 hours, or to 41F or below in 6 hours. CORRECTED- Discussed cooling methods with PIC. Food was moved in shallow pans and placed in the freezer to rapidly cool.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.15 Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: REPEAT: Observed wooden utensil used to put mustard on buns. Wood is not permitted for food-contact use. Replace utensil with something other than wood. PIC removed the wooden utensil from use.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.17 (A) Except as specified in ¶¶ (B), (C), and (D) of this section, wood and wood wicker may not be used as a FOOD-CONTACT SURFACE. (C)

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Observed handwashing sink with no paper towels provided (empty dispenser). CORRECTED- PIC refilled dispenser with paper towels.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with (A) Individual, disposable towels. (Pf)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed sanitizing sink of 3 compartment sink to have Cl concentration of 10ppm. CORRECTED- PIC remade sanitizing compartment to correct concentration.
4-501.114 (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the 2017 FDA Food Code. (P)

Observed 3 compartment sink set up as: wash, sanitize, rinse. PIC stated that it is used in the correct order, but is easier to use set up in this configuration. CORRECTED- Discussed correct order with PIC and provided education.

Observed cups being used as ice scoop at the shake station. Provide ice scoop with a handle to prevent bare hand contact with ice. Inspector will follow up in 10 days.
Reference 3-304.11 (A) FOOD shall only contact surfaces of EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned as specified
under Part 4-6 of this Code and SANITIZED as specified under Part 4-7 of this Code. (P)

Observed brown build up in the ice machine. Inspector will follow up in 10 days.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: Observed staff to go between food prep and other activities without washing hands or changing gloves. Hands should be washed after any activities that may contaminate hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 (I) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Observed kitchen handsink without paper towels available. Corrected by providing paper towels.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 (A) Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with individual, disposable towels.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11  Ketchup stored next to raw hamburger. Store raw meats away from ready-to-eat foods to protect from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed soda nozzle to be soiled. PIC then washed nozzle without sanitizing. Provided education and nozzles will be properly cleaned and sanitized.
4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: Observed milkshake cups being stored on towels. Observed condiments to be stored in cardboard boxes. All non-food contact surfaces should be designed to be easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 4-202.16 NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.
